Ten comments

The Black Cat

This tune is played in Rouen’s session, in Normandy. I don’t know anything about his origin.

↳ Posted by Anthony Picard on March 12th, 2016.

Re: The Black Cat

It’s a composition of Daniel Compton.

↳ Posted by Anthony Picard on April 7th, 2016.

Re: The Black Cat

Dmin is such a rich-sounding key .. like any minor key ! A nice change from the majors ..

↳ Posted by DFMontgomery on January 7th, 2018.

The Black Cat, X:2

Some variations from the Kitchen Jam Band.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on August 11th, 2018.

Re: The Black Cat

Recently reminded of this by the Kitchen Jam Band, they raised the point it’s a good Halloween jig, given the name and all …

Fiddle video, starts at about 1min in:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tAJeZuD080M

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on October 29th, 2018.

The Black Cat, X:3

A few alternatives, chords, and swung some of the notes. Could drop the rolls and replace with long slides.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on November 24th, 2018.

The Black Cat, X:5

From the playing of George Penk, Clyde Curley, Susan Songer, & Creighton Lindsay.

They play a few variations besides this, more specifically, sliding some of the notes in place of rolling.

Also updated the Kitchen Jam Band setting (X2) to be closer to their playing.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on October 31st, 2019.

The Black Cat, X:7

From the playing of The Contrarians.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on November 1st, 2019.

The Black Cat, X:8

From the playing of Lisa Ornstein & Dan Compton (the composer). They add in a few extra bars to the B Part each time through the tune.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on November 1st, 2019.

The Black Cat, X:10

From the playing of Asha.

They have a C Part, which seems to have been derived from the extra few bars of the Dan Compton’s B Part.

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on April 8th, 2023.
